invariants.status: specified direction; protocol details and verification gated
invariants.evidence: Intent precedes SQLite commit, external finalization precedes acknowledgement, and divergent or unprovable histories fence service. Crash, replay and restore rules require independent review before activation.
Triggers are only backstops. The contract requires an enforced boundary and verified coordinator proof and reconciliation; failure to establish them blocks operation.
An independently authenticated client binding must be compared with the resolver and independent authority before every operation; ambient selection alone is insufficient.
The contract binds verified artifacts, runtime, processing contracts, activation identity, canonical input and exact vector bytes, and blocks unclassified or incompatible state.

invariants.status: specified; enforcement and progress verification gated
invariants.evidence: Admitted mutators acquire the common external fence before SQLite writes; disclosure revalidates and enqueues under that fence. Deadlines and progress remain implementation gates.
Rebuild is exclusively store-wide, staging is non-queryable, activation follows full validation, and owner-crash recovery remains fenced and explicit.

The irrevocable point is enqueue to the authenticated intended recipient under the fence. Already enqueued bytes may arrive after deletion acknowledgement; capacity exhaustion fails without disclosure.

invariants.status: specified within trusted-local scope; broader isolation gated
invariants.evidence: Eligibility, current authorization and final candidates are checked under the snapshot and disclosure protocol. Untrusted-principal guarantees remain subject to the separate authority design.
Missing authority, enforceable fencing, immutable artifacts, compatible runtime or reliable reconciliation blocks the affected path rather than constituting an achieved protection.
